title: Marc Veasey's recent tweets address business advocacy and federal investigations | Dallas Republic
text:

By Dallas City Wire Feb 20, 2025 Rep. Marc Veasey, a longstanding representative of Texas's 33rd District in the U.S. Congress, recently shared his activities and views through a series of tweets. Veasey, who has been serving since 2013 after his tenure in the Texas House of Representatives, uses social media to communicate directly with constituents and the public.
On February 18, 2025, Rep. Veasey tweeted about his experience at Frida’s Tacolandia in Dallas as part of his "Marc Means Business" initiative. He expressed enthusiasm for engaging with local businesses by stating: "In Texas, we take #TacoTuesday seriously! On this edition of Marc Means Business, I stepped into the kitchen at Frida’s Tacolandia to cook and serve up some of the best food in Dallas. I’m taking what I learned back to Congress to better advocate for small businesses like…"
On February 19, 2025, Veasey addressed healthcare policy following a decision by national leaders. He remarked on social media: "Glad to hear that President Musk and Co-President Trump have agreed not to cut Medicaid. Someone should tell Speaker Johnson and the House GOP." This comment highlights ongoing discussions regarding Medicaid funding.
The following day, February 20, 2025, Veasey called attention to serious allegations against an official within ICE. His tweet stated: "James Rodden has exposed himself as a white supremacist while serving as ICE’s Assistant Chief Counsel. I am demanding answers, sending a letter of inquiry, and calling for a full investigation now." This reflects his stance on accountability within government agencies.
